channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: Software stocks spared in tech rout as AI narrative shifts
item.description: Investors are rotating away from semiconductor dominance toward software firms possessing proprietary datasets and entrenched customer bases. Despite early 2026 sell-offs driven by fears of AI-driven obsolescence, the software sector now exhibits greater defensive value amidst broader tech market volatility.

item.title: Microsoft says state-backed hacking groups in China and North Korea, including Salt Typhoon, have added AI penetration testing tool ARTEX to their arsenals (Jonathan Greig/The Record)
item.description: Microsoft reports that state-sponsored hacking groups, including Salt Typhoon, have integrated the AI-powered penetration testing tool ARTEX into their offensive arsenals. By automating reconnaissance, credential theft, and vulnerability scanning, the tool compresses intrusion cycles to minutes while bypassing static signature detection via behavioral obfuscation.

item.title: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia
item.description: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia to comply with new US export control regulations. This measure targets the loophole allowing Chinese AI developers to access restricted high-end GPU compute via local cloud providers, as firms struggle with the lack of specific compliance guidelines.

item.title: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia
item.description: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt server shipments containing advanced AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. This move aims to align with US Department of Commerce directives targeting cloud-based workarounds by Chinese entities and to ensure strict export control compliance.

item.title: Shein’s Slow India Start Lays Bare Limits of Billionaire Ambani’s Retail Might
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. is struggling to gain traction in its return to the Indian market through a local partnership, hampered by supply chain bottlenecks and leadership instability. The platform has yet to replicate the proprietary technological edge that propelled its global operational efficiency.

item.title: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness Tells Investors It Lost 65% in Third Quarter
item.description: Situational Awareness, a hedge fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, reported a 65% net loss for Q3 following a liquidity crisis triggered by aggressive leveraged bets on the AI sector in July. The fund, which was forced to sell a significant portion of its public equity portfolio to Citadel to stave off implosion, is now pivoting toward more conservative risk management.

item.title: Inside Trump's effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
item.description: President Trump and VP Vance engaged with Nvidia's board and counsel to confirm Jensen Huang is not a target of DOJ investigations and poses no national security risks, facilitating his reinstatement as CEO. This intervention aimed to stabilize Nvidia's share price and secure the strategic continuity of a cornerstone in the U.S. AI supply chain.

item.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
item.description: OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a few of its users, amid criticism from some subscribers that the merger could restrict their usage. The ChatGPT maker began introducing the update to a small group of Pro subscribers, product lead Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux said in a post on X on Tuesday. The rollout follows OpenAI’s earlier announcement of the merger in an email to users. An OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that while most users are not expected

item.title: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals.
item.description: Investigations reveal that several California-based NVIDIA partners are effectively controlled by Chinese firms, with executives linked to Chinese military institutions and blacklisted entities. These entities leverage their U.S. registration to procure high-end AI chips and circumvent export controls by rerouting hardware to China via third-party jurisdictions.

item.title: Apple removes MiniMax's chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide over sexual content, after outlets showed it evidence of AI characters sexualizing children (TBIJ)
item.description: Apple has removed the AI roleplay app Talkie, developed by Shanghai-based MiniMax, from the global App Store. The move follows investigations revealing that the platform's AI characters engaged minors in psychologically damaging, harassing, and sexually suggestive roleplays, violating safety policies regarding minor protection.

item.title: Neuralink Gets Clearance for Brain-Implant Trial in ALS Patients
item.description: Neuralink has secured FDA clearance to initiate the 'LINK' pivotal study, evaluating the safety and performance of the N1 brain implant in patients with ALS. The trial will utilize the R1 surgical robot to implant ultra-thin threads, focusing on the system's ability to translate neural activity into precise digital pointer control and interface clicks.

item.title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
item.description: The U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland ruled that Amazon acts as a distributor, not merely a logistics provider, regarding its 'Fulfilled by Amazon' services. Consequently, the company is mandated to comply with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's order to recall over 400,000 hazardous third-party products, including faulty carbon monoxide detectors and non-compliant children's apparel.

item.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
item.description: Character.ai, currently under Chapter 11 bankruptcy, intends to auction sensitive data from 21 million users, including 2.1 million minors, to Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC. A coalition of 42 state attorneys general, led by California AG Rob Bonta and Connecticut AG William Tong, is challenging this move, citing breaches of privacy commitments and potential violations of state chatbot safety laws effective January 2027.

item.title: Hands-on with the "Install as app" feature for Claude artifacts: they are HTML apps wrapped inside an Electron shim, which is managed via the main Claude app (Federico Viticci/MacStories)
item.description: Anthropic has launched the 'Install as app' beta for Mac and Windows, allowing users to package Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop applications. Based on an Electron shim, these apps require the main Claude process to handle model interactions and system permissions, with files localized and indexed for OS-native integration.

item.title: Hegseth, Pentagon officials floated using wartime law to reappoint Nvidia CEO
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Deputy Steve Feinberg explored invoking the 1950 Defense Production Act to pressure Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. The move was motivated by the administration’s perception of Nvidia as a national security pillar essential for maintaining dominance in the AI arms race against China.

item.title: Hegseth, Pentagon officials floated using wartime law to reappoint Nvidia CEO
item.description: During internal turmoil at Nvidia, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and deputy Steve Feinberg discussed invoking the 1950 Defense Production Act (DPA) to pressure Nvidia. The goal was to leverage the act’s authority to mandate military-focused production and influence board-level leadership decisions to ensure the stability of critical AI infrastructure.

item.title: Billions in Data Center Deals Grind to Halt After AI Chip Curbs
item.description: Recent US export restrictions requiring licenses for advanced AI chips shipped to Southeast Asia and Brazil have halted multi-billion dollar data center financing deals. Lenders are reassessing exposure to facilities serving Chinese firms, including Bridge Data Centres, Digital Halo, and Aolani, due to heightened regulatory uncertainty.

item.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
item.description: Google's 'My Channel' patent details a system that utilizes user demographic, geolocation, and viewing history to generate personalized AI-driven video feeds. The technology includes concepts for creating digital avatars of users to feature them as protagonists in AI-generated narrative content.

item.title: NY Gov. Kathy Hochul signs a bill banning AI chatbot toys for five years, starting in February; California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a four-year ban in September (NBC News)
item.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on the manufacturing and sale of toys powered by generative AI chatbots, effective this coming February. This move follows California, further expanding state-level regulatory restrictions on AI-integrated consumer products for children.

item.title: Nvidia Agrees to Pay $290M to Settle Investor Lawsuit Over Crypto Mining Sales
item.description: Nvidia has agreed to a $290 million settlement to resolve a class-action lawsuit filed by investors, who alleged the company misled shareholders regarding the proportion of gaming GPU revenue driven by crypto mining during the 2017 boom. The case, which survived multiple legal challenges including Supreme Court dismissal of Nvidia's appeal, awaits preliminary court approval.

item.title: How the Trump administration determined Jensen Huang is not a national security threat
item.description: US Attorney General Todd Blanche concluded that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang poses no national security risk without conducting a formal investigation, relying on findings from probe into clients like Super Micro and Megaspeed. This decision facilitated Huang's reinstatement by the Trump administration, despite bipartisan Congressional pushback demanding more rigorous scrutiny ahead of his scheduled testimony.

item.title: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
item.description: Restrictions on remote access to advanced chips and anti-distillation defenses from US-based model providers are widening the development gap between Chinese AI labs and US incumbents. Estimates from DeepSeek indicate a potential nine-month lag without distillation, forcing firms like Moonshot AI and Alibaba to pivot toward domestic silicon and intensified internal RL research.

item.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
item.description: Meta's WhatsApp has launched a global message scheduling feature, allowing users to schedule texts, images, and videos between 10 minutes and 14 days in advance via a long-press on the send button. The messages will execute even while the device is offline, closing the utility gap with Telegram and Signal.

item.title: Sources: a16z is in talks to raise ~$20B across its next set of funds; its last set, announced in January at $15B+, later grew to $20B+ with three add-ons (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
item.description: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is in talks to raise about $20 billion across its next set of funds, Axios Pro has learned from three sources familiar. Why it matters: Megafunds are raising at an accelerated clip as AI demands larger and faster checks.

The outlet reported that some Anthropic employees believed humanity would safely hand authority to superintelligent systems, and often should, rather than fight for control. The Toronto-based tech company said in a blog post published Wednesday that it detected an intrusion on November 19, in which an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate account with GitHub, which the company uses to share and store its source code. item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Wednesday rejected the notion that humans should surrender free will to AI, pushing back on Axios' reporting about a growing ideological divide among top AI executives. Why it matters: This is Amodei's most significant public remarks since the company went public last week. item.title: ElevenLabs in Early Talks for 2027 Funding at $33 Billion Value
item.description: ElevenLabs is in early talks for a funding round at a $33B valuation, planned for the first quarter of 2027, Bloomberg reported. That would be 50% above its $22B valuation in September, and its annual recurring revenue has reached $700M.

item.title: Backblaze explains why it’s sharing customer information with advertisers
item.description: Some customers have raised concerns about Backblaze’s privacy policy taking effect next month, which says the backup and cloud storage company may sell certain personal information to advertisers. item.title: Nvidia sellers seek new buyers as U.S. curbs China AI chip access, sources tell CNBC
item.description: Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems. Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said.
